title: The Pattern on the Cloth
fact_notes: オリジナル論説・架空事例。実在の歴史資料・調査・教育効果の実証ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: A student visiting a fictional craft exhibition stops in front of a piece of woven cloth.
sentences.ja: 架空の工芸展示を訪れる生徒が織物の前で立ち止まる。

sentences.en: The cloth contains a series of repeated shapes in different colors.
sentences.ja: 布には異なる色の繰り返し模様が並んでいる。

sentences.en: She initially believes that the craftsperson simply chose the pattern because it looked attractive.
sentences.ja: 当初、職人が見た目が魅力的だから模様を選んだだけだと思う。

sentences.en: A guide invites her to examine the way the cloth was made.
sentences.ja: 案内人は布の作り方を調べるよう促す。

sentences.en: The guide shows her a simple model of a weaving process using paper strips.
sentences.ja: 案内人は紙の帯を使った織りの過程の簡単な模型を見せる。

sentences.en: Some patterns are easier to produce when the strips are arranged in a particular sequence.
sentences.ja: 帯が特定の順序で配置されると作りやすい模様もある。

sentences.en: Changing the order can create a different appearance even when the same colors are used.
sentences.ja: 同じ色を使っても順番を変えると異なる外見が生まれる。

sentences.en: The student begins to recognize a relationship between the design and the method of production.
sentences.ja: 生徒はデザインと製作方法の関係に気づき始める。

sentences.en: She tries making two small examples with the materials provided by the guide.
sentences.ja: 案内人の用意した材料で小さな例を二つ作ってみる。

sentences.en: One arrangement produces the intended pattern without much difficulty.
sentences.ja: 一つの配置はあまり苦労せず意図した模様を生む。

sentences.en: The second requires more careful attention to the order of the strips.
sentences.ja: 二つ目は帯の順序により慎重な注意を必要とする。

sentences.en: The activity does not reproduce every skill needed to create an actual woven object.
sentences.ja: 活動は実際の織物を作るため必要な技能をすべて再現しない。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, the model encourages the student to look at the original cloth again.
sentences.ja: それでも模型は元の布を再び見るよう生徒を促す。

sentences.en: She notices details that previously seemed like simple decorative choices.
sentences.ja: 以前は単純な装飾上の選択に見えた細部に気づく。

sentences.en: The guide explains that a craftsperson may consider the available materials, the intended use and the appearance of a product at the same time.
sentences.ja: 職人は利用可能な材料、想定用途、製品の外見を同時に考えるかもしれないと案内人は説明する。

sentences.en: The fictional example does not claim that every traditional pattern has the same meaning or origin.
sentences.ja: 架空例はすべての伝統模様が同じ意味や由来を持つと主張しない。

sentences.en: A finished object can communicate something about the decisions involved in its creation.
sentences.ja: 完成品は制作に伴う判断について何かを伝え得る。

sentences.en: Understanding a method of production may change the way we appreciate a design.
sentences.ja: 製作方法を理解するとデザインの鑑賞方法が変わるかもしれない。

sentences.en: The beauty of a pattern need not be separated from the practical knowledge that made it possible.
sentences.ja: 模様の美しさは、それを可能にした実践知識から切り離す必要はない。

sentences.en: The cloth becomes an invitation to examine both art and technique.
sentences.ja: 布は芸術と技法の両方を調べる誘いになる。

vocabulary.definition: skill in making things by hand
state of being hard to do
intended to make something look attractive
place or cause from which something begins

questions.prompt: What does she initially assume about the pattern?
options: It was produced by the guide.
It was chosen only for its appearance.
questions.explanation_ja: 見た目だけで選んだと思う。

questions.prompt: What does the guide use in the model?
What can changing the order of the strips do?
options: Guarantee that all patterns are identical.
Produce a different appearance with the same colors.
Make the cloth impossible to examine.
questions.explanation_ja: 同じ色でも模様が変わる。

questions.prompt: How does the second arrangement differ?
options: It requires more attention to order.
It takes place outside the exhibition.

questions.prompt: What is a limitation of the model?
options: It exactly reproduces every professional technique.
It proves that all cloth is made identically.
It does not reproduce all the skills of real weaving.
questions.explanation_ja: 実際の技能すべては再現しない。

options: Only the color of the paper.

questions.prompt: Why avoid claiming that all patterns have the same origin?
options: The fictional example does not establish universal historical explanations.
A person who visits a gallery.
A particular way of doing something.
The appearance of a work is always unrelated to its production.
Understanding how objects are made can enrich our appreciation of their design.
Paper models prove every historical claim.
Crafts should be judged only by color.

grammar.focus: even when the same colors are used
needed to create an actual woven object

paraphrases.explanation_ja: 見た目を理由と考える。

paraphrases.rewrite: The same colors can produce a different pattern if arranged differently.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 色が同じでも配置で変化。

paraphrases.source: The activity does not reproduce every skill needed to create an actual woven object.
paraphrases.rewrite: The model does not demonstrate every skill required for real weaving.

paraphrases.source: The beauty of a pattern need not be separated from the practical knowledge that made it possible.
paraphrases.rewrite: The beauty of the pattern can be understood together with the knowledge behind it.

芸術と技法をまとめる。
